hypothesis: But reckoning time, whose million'd accidents, Creep in twixt vows, And change decrees of kings, Tan's sacred beauty, blunt the sharpest intense, Divert strong minds to the course of altering things. Alas, why fearing of time's tyranny? Might I not then say, Now I love you best, When I was certain o'er in certainty, Crowning the present, doubting of the rest?
